title: Unique generator-normalized finite scalar pullback chain map
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite extensions and let $\iota:E\to L$ be a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-embedding. For $F=E,L$, fix its valuation ring $\mathcal O_F$ and a uniformizer $\varpi_F$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$, work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], small relative to the universe of module sheaves. Put $R_{F,W}=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m)_W$ for $F=E,L$, with the canonical quotient projections [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the compatible quotient coefficient maps induced by the embedding [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and hence $j_W:R_{E,W}\to R_{L,W}$. Let $S_W$ be ordinary, uncompleted change of rings $M\mapsto R_{L,W}\otimes_{R_{E,W}}M$, sheafified, applied termwise to cochain complexes with differential $1\otimes d$ [def-pur-change-of-rings-complex, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $1\otimes x$ for the canonical sheafification-unit tensor section, not an assertion that arbitrary sections are globally pure [def-sfb-scalar-extension-pure-tensor-section]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any scheme morphism and $n\in\mathbf N$. The index $n$ denotes quotient exponent $n+1$. For $F=E,L$, put $P^F_{f,n}(P)=\operatorname{Res}_{\pi^F_{n+1}} f^*_{F,n+1}((\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^{n+1})_Y\otimes_{R_{F,Y}}P)$, with the ordinary finite module inverse image, all functors applied termwise [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Here $f^*$ on a section over $V\in Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ means its canonical pullback-unit section over $X\times_Y V$. There exists exactly one natural transformation of complex-valued functors
$$\alpha_n:S_X\circ P^E_{f,n}\longrightarrow P^L_{f,n}\circ S_Y$$
whose components are $R_{L,X}$-linear chain maps and which, for every complex $P$, degree $i$, object $V\in Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and $x\in P^i(V)$, satisfies
$$\alpha_n(P)^i\bigl(1\otimes f^*(1\otimes x)\bigr)=f^*\bigl(1\otimes(1\otimes x)\bigr).$$
Naturality is with respect to every chain map, without flatness, K-flatness, boundedness, constructibility or invertibility of $\ell$ on the schemes.

source.place: lemma-tensor-product-pullback (Tag 03EL), applied to the finite coefficient pullback and coefficient change; section-tensor-product for the balanced sheaf tensor construction. Project specialization: IntegralOperationsScalarComparisonModels.lean:112-124 and normalization:88-109.
source.note: Retained original parent proof step 2 (H1, 2026-10-26), as construction material for this unsplit statement, not a completed proof: For pullback at each finite quotient level, use the scalar tensor and inverse-image adjunction universal properties to define the map sending 1 tensor f*(1 tensor x) to f*(1 tensor (1 tensor x)). The balanced relations, restriction maps, and differentials commute with this formula. Pure tensors and the inverse-image adjunction force uniqueness and naturality. For tensor at each level, the balanced tensor universal property gives 1 tensor ((1 tensor x) tensor (1 tensor y)) mapping to (1 tensor (1 tensor x)) tensor (1 tensor (1 tensor y)). The signed total differential commutes by bidegree, and the coproduct universal property gives the total chain map and its uniqueness. These are exactly the two pre-existing holes; no new comparison assertion is introduced.

proof.text: Take the normalized natural chain transformation constructed by lem-pur-integral-scalar-pullback-level-construction. Its functors and generator equation are literally those in the present statement.

For a second normalized transformation, use natural-transformation extensionality and degreewise chain-map extensionality. The scalar_pullback_hom_ext lemma from the existing pullback-level-reduction module tests equality on exactly the normalized scalar/pullback/reduction unit generators. Both maps take each generator to the same prescribed target section. Thus the constructed transformation is unique.

theorem scalarPullbackLevel_existsUnique {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃! α : integralOperationsPullbackLevel l E f n ⋙
        (integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι X).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⟶
      (integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι Y).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        integralOperationsPullbackLevel l L f n,
      scalarPullbackLevelNormalization l E L ι f n α
